review_notes: I read the whole file and every use of its declarations across the repo (WeightedCoordinateExtraction, ReindexedFastCoefficientSection, FirstCoefficientLatticeCoordinates, NiltestBasepointNormalization). I grepped Mathlib's ToLin.lean and the rest of Mathlib for simp lemmas about `equivFun` or `toMatrix` of a reindexed basis. I found only toMatrix_reindexRange and Basis.reindex_apply / repr_reindex_apply, so the file's lemmas don't duplicate anything. I did not run Lean. The suggested simp attributes and generalizations are untested, and I have not checked whether other simp lemmas would conflict with them. The other declarations (realDenominatorGrid_comp and the sorted_basis_* lemmas) are plain implications or membership facts, and I made no simp recommendation for them.

findings.excerpt: (b.reindex e.symm).equivFun x = fun i => b.equivFun x (e i)
findings.problem: This is a canonical normalizing rewrite. It pushes `reindex` out of the coordinate map, and the right-hand side is strictly simpler. It is not tagged `@[simp]`, and Mathlib has no simp lemma for `(b.reindex e).equivFun`. Every use therefore has to name it by hand, as in `rw [..., basis_reindex_equivFun]` and `simpa only [basis_reindex_equivFun] using ...`. The statement is also fixed to the shape `b.reindex e.symm` with `e : Equiv.Perm ι`. As a simp lemma it would not fire on `b.reindex e`, nor on a reindex along a general `ι ≃ κ`. The sibling lemma `basis_reindex_equivFun_symm` in NiltestBasepointNormalization is stated for `e : ι ≃ κ` and is also not simp, so the two forms are inconsistent.
findings.proposed_change: State the lemma for general `e : ι ≃ κ` in the canonical form `(b.reindex e).equivFun x = fun i => b.equivFun x (e.symm i)`. Tag it `@[simp]`. Keep the current `e.symm` statement as a corollary if needed, or let `Equiv.symm_symm` handle it. Consider doing the same for `equivFun.symm` in NiltestBasepointNormalization, so that `simp` can normalize reindexed coordinates without a named lemma.
findings.benefit: Callers such as `reindexCoordinateSection_right_inverse` and `exists_reindexed_fast_coefficient_section` could use plain `simp` instead of hand-listing the lemma. The rule would also fire on any `b.reindex e` goal, not only the `e.symm` form. The orientation is safe because `reindex` is removed and the right-hand side is smaller.

(b.reindex e).equivFun.symm x = b.equivFun.symm (fun i => x (e i))

findings.excerpt:
LinearMap.toMatrix (b.reindex e.symm) (b.reindex e.symm) f i j =
      LinearMap.toMatrix b b f (e i) (e j)
findings.problem: This entry-wise formula for `toMatrix` in a reindexed basis is the natural simp normal form. The LHS has a `reindex`, the RHS is in the original basis, and the rewrite terminates. It is not a simp lemma, so the three `sorted_basis_*` proofs and `WeightedCoordinateExtraction` call it explicitly with `rw`. It is also restricted to `e : Equiv.Perm ι` and to the `e.symm` form, so a `b.reindex e` with a general equivalence would not match. It is also stated only for the same reindexed basis on both sides, so a simp lemma for the `toMatrix` of a reindexed domain or codomain alone would need a separate statement.
findings.proposed_change: Generalize to `e : ι ≃ κ` and state it as `LinearMap.toMatrix (b.reindex e) (b.reindex e) f i j = LinearMap.toMatrix b b f (e.symm i) (e.symm j)`. Tag it `@[simp]`. Keep the current `e.symm` form as a corollary only if downstream code needs it. The `sorted_basis_*` proofs could then start with `simp only [basis_reindex_toMatrix]`, or plain `simp`.
findings.benefit: Matrix entries of reindexed bases get one canonical form. Downstream goals, for example in `exists_lattice_ready_firstCoefficient_basis`, would reduce to `toMatrix b b` entries by `simp` without the caller knowing the lemma name. The change also removes the arbitrary `Perm`/`e.symm` restriction from the rewrite rule.
